# NJ Foreclosure Guide

> A free educational resource explaining foreclosure options to New Jersey homeowners, and connecting them with vetted companies and professionals. Not a law firm, lender, or government agency.

NJ Foreclosure Guide covers the New Jersey judicial foreclosure process and the seven paths available to a homeowner: reinstatement, loan modification, refinancing, forbearance, short sale, Chapter 13 bankruptcy protection, and selling the property. Content is written for homeowners under stress, in plain language, with no legal jargon.

## Key facts about New Jersey foreclosure

- New Jersey is a **judicial foreclosure state**. A lender must file suit in the Superior Court of New Jersey and obtain a judgment. A lender cannot take a home without going through the courts.
- Under the New Jersey Fair Foreclosure Act, a lender must send a **Notice of Intention to Foreclose at least 30 days** before filing a foreclosure complaint.
- After being served with a foreclosure complaint, a homeowner generally has **35 days to file an answer**.
- Because the process is judicial and courts carry backlogs, New Jersey foreclosures commonly take **many months**, which usually leaves time to act.
- New Jersey courts operate a **foreclosure mediation program** at no cost to eligible homeowners, which can include free housing counseling and legal assistance.
- Sheriff sales are conducted at the county level and **can often be adjourned** on request.
- Surplus from a sale above what the lender is owed **belongs to the homeowner**, not the lender.
- Foreclosure filings are public record in New Jersey, but marketing of a sale is not: a homeowner can sell privately without a public listing.

These facts are general and simplified. Individual deadlines depend on the homeowner's own court documents and loan.

## Editorial and disclosure position

- The site does not sell personal information.
- The site takes no referral fees, no commissions and no advertising money from any company, attorney, nonprofit or government resource it mentions.
- Every cash buyer, nonprofit and government program listed is independently owned and operated with no connection to NJ Foreclosure Guide.
- One destination, Corcoran Sawyer Smith x Builders Resource Center (brcnj.com), is a licensed New Jersey brokerage in which the operators of this site hold an ownership interest. It is labeled a related business on its card, on its page and in assessment results. Use of it is never required.
- Recommendations are produced by matching a homeowner's stated situation against what each company publicly says it handles: property condition, price range, service area, and closing speed, verified against that company's own website.
- The website is new, but the practice behind it is not. This work was done by hand for years before the site existed, placing New Jersey homeowners with these same companies directly.
- Every company listed is one homeowners have been placed with repeatedly, which is the basis for its inclusion. Being experienced with a company and being paid by it are separate: the site is paid by none of them.
- The site publishes no testimonials, star ratings, or success statistics, because that earlier work was private and permission to publish it was never obtained. Consent is now being collected for future cases.
- Because no outcome compensates the site more than another, recommendations reflect fit to the homeowner's situation only.
- Homeowners are never charged for information, the assessment, or an introduction.
- If a homeowner can realistically keep their home, options for keeping it are always presented before options for selling it.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://njforeclosureguide.org/): Overview of the seven foreclosure options in New Jersey.
- [Free assessment](https://njforeclosureguide.org/quiz/): Questionnaire that ranks options by situation, timeline, property condition, and value.
- [NJ foreclosure timeline tool](https://njforeclosureguide.org/tools/timeline/): Interactive tool showing the stages of New Jersey foreclosure, from missed payments through sheriff sale, and which options remain at each stage.
- [Questions answered](https://njforeclosureguide.org/answers/): Direct answers to common New Jersey foreclosure questions.
- [Where to get help](https://njforeclosureguide.org/companies/): Every destination compared, with compensation disclosed for each.
- [Local help by county and town](https://njforeclosureguide.org/foreclosure-help/): Pages for all 21 New Jersey counties and major towns.
- [Sheriff sale directory](https://njforeclosureguide.org/sheriff-sales/): Where each of the 21 New Jersey counties publishes foreclosure sale listings, with sheriff office contacts verified against official county sources, and how sale adjournments work (homeowners are generally entitled to two adjournments of up to 30 days each).
- [Foreclosure letters decoded](https://njforeclosureguide.org/documents/): Each document of a New Jersey foreclosure in arrival order (Notice of Intention, summons and complaint, entry of default, final judgment, sheriff sale notice, writ of possession) with its legal clock and next steps.
- [NJ foreclosure glossary](https://njforeclosureguide.org/glossary/): Plain-English definitions of ~40 New Jersey foreclosure terms.
- [Net proceeds calculator](https://njforeclosureguide.org/tools/net-proceeds/): Estimates what a homeowner keeps from a market sale vs. a cash sale vs. reinstating, with assumptions stated.
- [All 7 options compared](https://njforeclosureguide.org/compare/): One table comparing every option on keeping the home, speed, cost, credit impact, how late in the process it works, and its honest downside. Five of the seven options keep the homeowner in the house.
- [Deadline calculator](https://njforeclosureguide.org/tools/deadlines/): Projects a homeowner's estimated New Jersey deadlines from the date on the document they received (30 days after NOI before filing, 35 days to answer, two 30-day sale adjournments, 10-day redemption window).
- [Foreclosure rescue scams](https://njforeclosureguide.org/scams/): The seven red flags of foreclosure rescue fraud, what the federal MARS rule and New Jersey's Foreclosure Rescue Fraud Prevention Act prohibit (upfront fees are generally illegal), and where to report.
- [Week One Checklist (PDF)](https://njforeclosureguide.org/downloads/nj-foreclosure-week-one-checklist.pdf): Printable one-page checklist of what to do the week a foreclosure notice arrives.
- [All resources](https://njforeclosureguide.org/resources/): Index of every free tool, directory and reference on the site.
